## How does a language model produce the next token?

A large language model (LLM) receives a sequence of tokens and computes a probability distribution to predict what comes next. This apparently simple operation relies on data, numerical representations, attention mechanisms, and a learning objective.

**LLM Lab connects these mechanisms to their mathematical explanations and observable behaviour.** The goal is not to trust an intuition because a diagram looks convincing: it is to understand what a component computes, verify what can be tested, and identify what remains an assumption or limitation.

## A six-step learning thread

The sidebar follows a chain of understanding: **from data to representations, from representations to a prediction, then from prediction to learning and evaluation**. This is a suggested route, not a mandatory reading order.

:::: {.learning-route}
::: {.route-step}
**1 · Get oriented**

What problem does an LLM solve? Where do Transformers, other model families, and the main lifecycle stages fit?

[System overview](transformer.qmd) · [Historical landmarks](transformer-history.qmd)
:::
::: {.route-step}
**2 · Prepare the data**

How do documents become usable text, then tokens, token IDs, and training examples?

[Text, tokenization, and data](text-data.qmd) · [Training examples](training-examples.qmd)
:::
::: {.route-step}
**3 · Build representations**

How do IDs become tensors and vectors, then representations that depend on context?

[Tensors](tensors.qmd) · [Embedding space](embedding-space.qmd) · [Contextualized representations](contextualized-representations.qmd)
:::
::: {.route-step}
**4 · Compute a prediction**

How does the model combine information across positions and transform representations into scores and probabilities?

[Attention and masking](queries-keys-values.qmd) · [Logits and probabilities](logits.qmd)
:::
::: {.route-step}
**5 · Learn the parameters**

How do we quantify the gap between predictions and targets, compute gradients, and update parameters?

[Likelihood and cross-entropy](likelihood.qmd) · [Loss and gradients](loss.qmd)
:::
::: {.route-step}
**6 · Evaluate and continue**

How do we assess performance, analyze errors, and decide what to do next? Generation is introduced in the system overview; its dedicated deep dive remains to be developed.

[Experimental evaluation](experimental-evaluation.qmd) · [Exercises](exercises.qmd)
:::
::::

::: {.callout-note}
**Current scope.** This route organizes the content currently available; it does not claim that a complete GPT has already been implemented. Detailed generation, reproducible pretraining, and adaptation of a pretrained model remain distinct workstreams beyond the conceptual route.
:::

## Choose your starting point

These three approaches complement one another; they are not mandatory stages. Follow the main thread, start with a specific question, or investigate a mechanism without reading every preceding page.

:::: {.learning-grid}
::: {.learning-card}
<span class="step">01 · BIG PICTURE</span>

### Understand the system before the details

Follow the broad flow of information: from text to tokens, from representations to prediction, and from prediction error to learning. This first view focuses on roles and relationships rather than derivations.

**Start here:** a visual overview, then the [Transformer overview](transformer.qmd).
:::
::: {.learning-card}
<span class="step">02 · GUIDED BUILD</span>

### Follow the construction of a small model

Start with data and training examples, then connect representations, attention, the loss function, optimization, and generation. Code pages and tests help compare explanations with actual computation.

**Start here:** [text and data](text-data.qmd), then [training examples](training-examples.qmd).
:::
::: {.learning-card}
<span class="step">03 · DEEP DIVE</span>

### Investigate a specific question

Explore a definition, derivation, tensor shapes, an assumption, a counterexample, or an implementation. Each detour should state its prerequisites and provide a route back to the big picture.

**Start here:** [applied mathematical foundations](mathematical-foundations.qmd) or [tensors and shapes](tensors.qmd).
:::
::::

## Verify, do not only visualize

A page may combine intuition, mathematical derivation, code, tests, and experiments. These provide different kinds of evidence:

- a diagram makes a structure readable but does not prove a property;
- a derivation establishes a result under explicit assumptions;
- a test checks the cases it covers but does not by itself prove a general rule;
- an experiment compares configurations under a documented protocol, metrics, and limitations.

Pages distinguish available explanations, code that has actually been tested, and work that remains planned.

## Guided build and intended scope

The guided path aims to build a small decoder-only GPT from randomly initialized parameters: data and tokenizer, training examples, representations, architecture, objective, optimization, validation, and generation. Adapting a pretrained model (classification, instruction tuning, LoRA, quantization) is a separate branch.

The complete path, prerequisites, and evidence criteria are documented in the [curriculum map](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/docs/full-curriculum-plan.md) and [learning path](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/docs/learning-path.md). **A page existing does not mean its implementation, tests, or rendering have been validated**: the sidebar reflects currently available content, not the full intended programme.

## Further resources

- [3Blue1Brown — Transformers](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LPZh9BOjkQs&t=10s): visual intuition and the big picture.
- [Sebastian Raschka — LLMs from Scratch](https://github.com/rasbt/LLMs-from-scratch/): a detailed model-building path and associated code.
- [Jay Alammar — The Illustrated Transformer](https://jalammar.github.io/illustrated-transformer/) and [The Illustrated GPT-2](https://jalammar.github.io/illustrated-gpt2/): visual explanations of model mechanisms.
- [Annotated bibliography](../references.qmd): scientific sources, technical documentation, and teaching resources, with their roles and limitations.
